title: Business Process
description: Schema for Business Process entries in technehub-labs/dea-catalog-processes. Mirrors technehub-labs/dea-metamodel/schemas/entities/process.json (v3.0.0-alpha). The Business Process is the specialization of the OpenDEAM Process kernel (dea:Process in dea-metamodel Core; dea:entity-process in the OpenDEAM root model) for the Business Architecture and Business Operations use cases (CR-MM-PROC-01; CR-AR-FMWK-01; CR-BP-SPEC-BP-01). Sub-classifications (operational / support / management; carried by process_intent) are catalog-internal and do not promote to root-model entities. CR-BP-03 ADDS the process_type (5-value Mintzberg), process_specialization (inheritance), relationships (canonical OpenDEA dea:composes + dea:realizes), and identity sub-block fields ADDITIVELY; existing fields are preserved and existing entries continue to validate.

process_intent.description: Work-character axis. Preserved from CR-BP-01 (operational / support / management). Describes what the process is doing.

process_audience.description: ECF domain the process serves. Preserved from CR-BP-01. process_audience is a single-axis audience classification (CG-004 §10); it is NOT a full ECF coordinate (Domain x Lifecycle Stage) — that lives in Process Context (CR-BP-02).

process_type.description: 5-component classification (Mintzberg). NEW in CR-BP-03. Where the process sits in the enterprise process landscape. Default: 'core' (the canonical classification for L2 Business Process entries). This is a CATALOG CLASSIFICATION (per CR-BP-03 §3), not a new ontology; the semantic entity remains dea:BusinessProcess regardless of process_type. See classifications/process-types.yaml for the controlled vocabulary.

process_specialization.description: Optional: list of parent process ids this entry specializes (inheritance / pattern-based refinement). NEW in CR-BP-03. Multi-inheritance is permitted. The authoritative dea:specializes relationship in the metamodel continues to govern the kernel + specialization discipline (CR-MM-PROC-01); this field is a catalog-level annotation for navigation and governance. See classifications/process-specializations.yaml for the controlled vocabulary of patterns.

specialization_pattern.description: Optional: free-text pattern label (e.g. 'by-customer-segment', 'by-region', 'by-product-line', 'by-tier', 'by-compliance-regime'). NEW in CR-BP-03. See classifications/process-specializations.yaml for the controlled vocabulary.

relationships.description: Canonical OpenDEA relationships (NEW in CR-BP-03). The relationship shape uses dea:composes for structural decomposition and dea:realizes for capability realization. This is the AUTHORITATIVE form; the legacy parent_process / child_processes / capabilities_delivered fields below are preserved as migration aliases and shall not remain authoritative (a follow-on migration validator CR-BP-03A will surface entries that have only the old fields).

composes.description: Canonical OpenDEA dea:composes: the L2 Business Process structurally composes other L2 Business Processes. Structural composition means part-of structure; containment; hierarchical decomposition; no implied sequence, execution, or organizational ownership.

realizes.description: Canonical OpenDEA dea:realizes: the L2 Business Process realizes one or more Business Capabilities. The realizes relationship is orthogonal to composes; a process may realize a capability without composing it, and compose another process without realizing any capability directly.

identity.description: Process identity sub-block (NEW in CR-BP-03; mirrors schemas/identity.schema.json inline to avoid a remote $ref). Tests a process by name + description + trigger + outcome + evidence, not by name alone. Optional at the schema level (entries without identity are admitted but flagged for review in the contribution report).

verb.description: Action verb (imperative; singular; TitleCase). E.g. Manage, Deliver, Onboard, Operate, Design, Govern. The verb should match the verb in the process name (the name is typically '<verb> <object>').

object.description: The noun being acted on (TitleCase). E.g. Customer, Service, Order, Portfolio, Data, Risk. The object should match the noun in the process name.

outcome_statement.description: Outcome statement (the description-of-record). Describes what the process achieves — not what it does.

trigger.description: What initiates the process. Used by the contribution report to cross-check the identity (BP-ARC-ID-002).

outcome.description: What the process produces. Used by the contribution report to cross-check the identity (BP-ARC-ID-003).

parent_process.description: Migration alias (preserved). Use relationships.composes instead in new entries.

child_processes.description: Migration alias (preserved). Use relationships.composes instead in new entries.

capabilities_delivered.description: Migration alias (preserved). Use relationships.realizes instead in new entries.

ecfConformance.description: ECF Conformance Gate manifest (CR-ECF-CG-001..004). Declares the catalog's CONFORMANT-WITH-EXTENSION status and the canonical ECF references that resolve. Optional at schema level; scripts/check_ecf_conformance.py enforces presence on every canonical process entry. Note: process_audience is NOT an ECF Coordinate; it is a single-axis audience classification (CG-004 §10). The canonical ECF reference (when present) lives in this ecfConformance block.
